verses.zh: 五旬节到了，门徒都聚集在一处。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all together in one place.
notes: Grk “And” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic. Greek style often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” but English style does not.

verses.zh: 忽然，从天上有响声下来，好像一阵大风吹过，充满了他们所坐的屋子，
verses.en: Suddenly[NOTE:1] a sound[NOTE:2] like a violent wind blowing[NOTE:3] came from heaven[NOTE:4] and filled the entire house where they were sitting.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated for stylistic reasons. It occurs as part of the formula καὶ ἐγένετο (kai egeneto) which is often left untranslated in Luke-Acts because it is redundant in contemporary English. Here it is possible (and indeed necessary) to translate ἐγένετο as “came” so that the initial clause of the English translation contains a verb; nevertheless the translation of the conjunction καί is not necessary.
Or “a noise.”

While φέρω (pherō) generally refers to movement from one place to another with the possible implication of causing the movement of other objects, in Acts 2:2 φέρομαι (pheromai) should probably be understood in a more idiomatic sense of “blowing” since it is combined with the noun for wind (πνοή, pnoē).
Or “from the sky.” The Greek word οὐρανός (ouranos) may be translated “sky” or “heaven” depending on the context.

verses.zh: 又有舌头如火焰显现出来，分开落在他们各人头上。
verses.en: And tongues spreading out like a fire[NOTE:1] appeared to them and came to rest on each one of them.
notes: Or “And divided tongues as of fire.” The precise meaning of διαμερίζομαι (diamerizomai) in Acts 2:3 is difficult to determine. The meaning could be “tongues as of fire dividing up one to each person,” but it is also possible that the individual tongues of fire were divided (“And divided tongues as of fire appeared”). The translation adopted in the text (“tongues spreading out like a fire”) attempts to be somewhat ambiguous.

verses.zh: 他们就都被圣灵充满，按着圣灵所赐的口才说起别国的话来。
verses.en: All[NOTE:1] of them were filled with the Holy Spirit, and they began to speak in other languages[NOTE:2] as the Spirit enabled them.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “And all.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.

Other languages. Acts 2:6-7 indicates that these were languages understandable to the hearers, a diverse group from “every nation under heaven.”tn The Greek term is γλώσσαις (glōssais), the same word used for the tongues of fire.
Grk “just as the spirit gave them to utter.” The verb ἀποφθέγγομαι (apophthengomai) was used of special utterances in Classical Greek (BDAG 125 s.v.).

verses.zh: 那时，有虔诚的犹太人从天下各国来，住在耶路撒冷。
verses.en: Now there were devout Jews[NOTE:1] from every nation under heaven residing in Jerusalem.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “Jews, devout men.” It is possible that only men are in view here in light of OT commands for Jewish men to make a pilgrimage to Jerusalem at various times during the year (cf. Exod 23:17; 34:23; Deut 16:16). However, other evidence seems to indicate that both men and women might be in view. Luke 2:41-52 shows that whole families would make the temporary trip to Jerusalem. In addition, it is probable that the audience consisted of families who had taken up permanent residence in Jerusalem. The verb κατοικέω (katoikeō) normally means “reside” or “dwell,” and archaeological evidence from tombs in Jerusalem does indicate that many families immigrated to Jerusalem permanently (see B. Witherington, Acts, 135); this would naturally include women. Also, the word ἀνήρ (anēr), which usually does mean “male” or “man” (as opposed to woman), sometimes is used generically to mean “a person” (BDAG 79 s.v. 2; cf. Matt 12:41). Given this evidence, then, it is conceivable that the audience in view here is not individual male pilgrims but a mixed group of men and women.
Grk “Now there were residing in Jerusalem Jews, devout men from every nation under heaven.”map For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 这声音一响，众人都来聚集，各人听见门徒用众人的乡谈说话，就甚纳闷；
verses.en: When this sound[NOTE:1] occurred, a crowd gathered and was in confusion[NOTE:2] because each one heard them speaking in his own language.
notes: Or “this noise.”
Or “was bewildered.”

verses.zh: 都惊讶希奇说：「看哪，这说话的不都是加利利人吗？
verses.en: Completely baffled, they said,[NOTE:1] “Aren’t[NOTE:2] all these who are speaking Galileans?
notes: Grk “They were astounded and amazed, saying.” The two imperfect verbs, ἐξίσταντο (existanto) and ἐθαύμαζον (ethaumazon), show both the surprise and the confusion on the part of the hearers. The verb ἐξίσταντο (from ἐξίστημι, existēmi) often implies an illogical perception or response (BDAG 350 s.v. ἐξίστημι): “to be so astonished as to almost fail to comprehend what one has experienced” (L&N 25.218).

Grk “Behold, aren’t all these.” The Greek word ἰδού (idou) at the beginning of this statement has not been translated because it has no exact English equivalent here, but adds interest and emphasis (BDAG 468 s.v. 1).

verses.zh: 我们各人怎么听见他们说我们生来所用的乡谈呢？
verses.en: And how is it that each one of us hears them[NOTE:1] in our own native language?[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “we hear them, each one of us.”
Grk “in our own language in which we were born.”

verses.zh: 我们帕提亚人、米底亚人、以拦人，和住在美索不达米亚、犹太、加帕多家、本都、亚细亚、
verses.en: Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and residents of Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and the province of Asia,[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “Asia”; in the NT this always refers to the Roman province of Asia. The Roman province of Asia made up about one-third of modern Asia Minor and was on the western side of it. Asia lay to the west of the region of Phrygia and Galatia. The words “the province of” are supplied to indicate to the modern reader that this does not refer to the continent of Asia.

verses.zh: 弗吕家、旁非利亚、埃及的人，并靠近古利奈的利比亚一带地方的人，从罗马来的客旅中，或是犹太人，或是进犹太教的人，
verses.en: Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya near Cyrene,[NOTE:1] and visitors from Rome,[NOTE:2]
notes: According to BDAG 595 s.v. Λιβύη, the western part of Libya, Libya Cyrenaica, is referred to here (see also Josephus, Ant. 16.6.1 [16.160] for a similar phrase).
For location see JP4-A1.

verses.zh: 克里特和阿拉伯人，都听见他们用我们的乡谈，讲说　神的大作为。」
verses.en: both Jews and proselytes,[NOTE:1] Cretans and Arabs—we hear them speaking in our own languages about the great deeds God has done!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Proselytes refers to Gentile (i.e., non-Jewish) converts to Judaism.
Or “God’s mighty works.” Here the genitive τοῦ θεοῦ (tou theou) has been translated as a subjective genitive.

verses.zh: 众人就都惊讶猜疑，彼此说：「这是甚么意思呢？」
verses.en: All were astounded and greatly confused, saying to one another, “What does this mean?”

verses.zh: 还有人讥诮说：「他们无非是新酒灌满了。」
verses.en: But others jeered at the speakers,[NOTE:1] saying, “They are drunk on new wine!”[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “the speakers” are not in the Greek text, but have been supplied for clarity. Direct objects were frequently omitted in Greek when clear from the context.
New wine refers to a new, sweet wine in the process of fermentation.tn Grk “They are full of new wine!”

verses.zh: 彼得和十一个使徒站起，高声说：「犹太人和一切住在耶路撒冷的人哪，这件事你们当知道，也当侧耳听我的话。
verses.en: But Peter stood up[NOTE:1] with the eleven, raised his voice, and addressed them: “You men of Judea[NOTE:2] and all you who live in Jerusalem,[NOTE:3] know this[NOTE:4] and listen carefully to what I say.
notes: Grk “standing up.” The participle σταθείς (statheis) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

Or “You Jewish men.” “Judea” is preferred here because it is paired with “Jerusalem,” a location. This suggests locality rather than ethnic background is the primary emphasis in the context. As for “men,” the Greek term here is ἀνήρ (anēr), which only exceptionally is used in a generic sense of both males and females. In this context, where “all” who live in Jerusalem are addressed, it is conceivable that this is a generic usage, although it can also be argued that Peter’s remarks were addressed primarily to the men present, even if women were there.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Grk “let this be known to you.”

verses.zh: 你们想这些人是醉了；其实不是醉了，因为时候刚到巳初。
verses.en: In spite of what you think, these men are not drunk,[NOTE:1] for it is only nine o’clock in the morning.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “These men are not drunk, as you suppose.”
Grk “only the third hour.”

verses.zh: 这正是先知约珥所说的：
verses.en: But this is what was spoken about through the prophet Joel:[NOTE:1]
notes: Note how in the quotation that follows all genders, ages, and classes are included. The event is like a hope Moses expressed in Num 11:29.

verses.zh: 神说：在末后的日子，我要将我的灵浇灌凡有血气的。你们的儿女要说预言；你们的少年人要见异象；老年人要做异梦。
verses.en: ‘And in the last days[NOTE:1] it will be,’ God says,‘that I will pour out my Spirit on all people,[NOTE:2] and your sons and your daughters will prophesy,and your young men will see visions,and your old men will dream dreams.
notes: The phrase in the last days is not quoted from Joel, but represents Peter’s interpretive explanation of the current events as falling “in the last days.”
Grk “on all flesh.”

verses.zh: 在那些日子，我要将我的灵浇灌我的仆人和使女，他们就要说预言。
verses.en: Even on my servants,[NOTE:1] both men and women,I will pour out my Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “slaves.” Although this translation frequently renders δοῦλος (doulos) as “slave,” the connotation is often of one who has sold himself into slavery; in a spiritual sense, the idea is that of becoming a slave of God or of Jesus Christ voluntarily. The voluntary notion is conspicuous here; hence the translation “servants.” In any case, the word does not bear the connotation of a free individual serving another. BDAG notes that “‘servant’ for ‘slave’ is largely confined to Biblical transl. and early American times…in normal usage at the present time the two words are carefully distinguished” (BDAG 260 s.v.). One good translation is “bondservant” (sometimes found in the ASV for δοῦλος) in that it often indicates one who sells himself into slavery to another. But as this is archaic, few today understand its force.

The words and they will prophesy in Acts 2:18 are not quoted from Joel 2:29 at this point but are repeated from earlier in the quotation (Acts 2:17) for emphasis. Tongues speaking is described as prophecy, just like intelligible tongues are described in 1 Cor 14:26-33.

verses.zh: 在天上，我要显出奇事；在地下，我要显出神迹；有血，有火，有烟雾。
verses.en: And I will perform wonders in the sky[NOTE:1] aboveand miraculous signs[NOTE:2] on the earth below,blood and fire and clouds of smoke.
notes: Or “in the heaven.” The Greek word οὐρανός (ouranos) may be translated “sky” or “heaven” depending on the context. Here, in contrast to “the earth below,” a reference to the sky is more likely.
Here the context indicates the miraculous nature of the signs mentioned; this is made explicit in the translation.

verses.zh: 日头要变为黑暗，月亮要变为血；这都在主大而明显的日子未到以前。
verses.en: The sun will be changed to darknessand the moon to bloodbefore the great and glorious[NOTE:1] day of the Lord comes.
notes: Or “and wonderful.”

verses.zh: 到那时候，凡求告主名的，就必得救。
verses.en: And then[NOTE:1] everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “And it will be that.”
A quotation from Joel 2:28-32.

verses.zh: 「以色列人哪，请听我的话：　神藉着拿撒勒人耶稣在你们中间施行异能、奇事、神迹，将他证明出来，这是你们自己知道的。
verses.en: “Men of Israel,[NOTE:1] listen to these words: Jesus the Nazarene, a man clearly attested to you by God with powerful deeds,[NOTE:2] wonders, and miraculous signs[NOTE:3] that God performed among you through him, just as you yourselves know—
notes: Or “Israelite men,” although this is less natural English. The Greek term here is ἀνήρ (anēr), which only exceptionally is used in a generic sense of both males and females. In this context, it is conceivable that this is a generic usage, although it can also be argued that Peter’s remarks were addressed primarily to the men present, even if women were there.
Or “miraculous deeds.”
Again, the context indicates the miraculous nature of these signs, and this is specified in the translation.

verses.zh: 他既按着　神的定旨先见被交与人，你们就藉着无法之人的手，把他钉在十字架上，杀了。
verses.en: this man, who was handed over by the predetermined plan and foreknowledge of God, you executed[NOTE:1] by nailing him to a cross at the hands of Gentiles.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “you killed.”

Grk “at the hands of lawless men.” At this point the term ἄνομος (anomos) refers to non-Jews who live outside the Jewish (Mosaic) law, rather than people who broke any or all laws including secular laws. Specifically it is a reference to the Roman soldiers who carried out Jesus’ crucifixion.

verses.zh: 神却将死的痛苦解释了，叫他复活，因为他原不能被死拘禁。
verses.en: But God raised him up,[NOTE:1] having released[NOTE:2] him from the pains[NOTE:3] of death because it was not possible for him to be held in its power.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “Whom God raised up.”
Or “having freed.”
The term translated pains is frequently used to describe pains associated with giving birth (see Rev 12:2). So there is irony here in the mixed metaphor.
Or “for him to be held by it” (in either case, “it” refers to death’s power).

verses.zh: 大卫指着他说：「我看见主常在我眼前；他在我右边，叫我不至于摇动。
verses.en: For David says about him,‘I saw the Lord always in front of me,[NOTE:1] for he is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken.
notes: Or “always before me.”

verses.zh: 所以，我心里欢喜，我的灵（原文是舌）快乐；并且我的肉身要安居在指望中。
verses.en: Therefore my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced;my body[NOTE:1] also will live in hope,
notes: Grk “my flesh.”

verses.zh: 因你必不将我的灵魂撇在阴间，也不叫你的圣者见朽坏。
verses.en: because you will not leave my soul in Hades,[NOTE:1] nor permit your Holy One to experience[NOTE:2] decay.
notes: Or “will not abandon my soul to Hades.” Often “Hades” is the equivalent of the Hebrew term Sheol, the place of the dead.
Grk “to see,” but the literal translation of the phrase “to see decay” could be misunderstood to mean simply “to look at decay,” while here “see decay” is really figurative for “experience decay.”

verses.zh: 你已将生命的道路指示我，必叫我因见你的面（或译：叫我在你面前）得着满足的快乐。
verses.en: You have made known to me the paths of life;you will make me full of joy with your presence.’[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Ps 16:8-11.

verses.zh: 「弟兄们！先祖大卫的事，我可以明明地对你们说：他死了，也葬埋了，并且他的坟墓直到今日还在我们这里。
verses.en: “Brothers,[NOTE:1] I can speak confidently[NOTE:2] to you about our forefather[NOTE:3] David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
notes: Since this represents a continuation of the address beginning in v.14 and continued in v. 22, “brothers” has been used here rather than a generic expression like “brothers and sisters.”
Peter’s certainty is based on well-known facts.
Or “about our noted ancestor,” “about the patriarch.”

verses.zh: 大卫既是先知，又晓得　神曾向他起誓，要从他的后裔中立一位坐在他的宝座上，
verses.en: So then, because[NOTE:1] he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn to him with an oath to seat one of his descendants[NOTE:2] on his throne,[NOTE:3]
notes: The participles ὑπάρχων (huparchōn) and εἰδώς (eidōs) are translated as causal adverbial participles.

Grk “one from the fruit of his loins.” “Loins” is the traditional translation of ὀσφῦς (osphus), referring to the male genital organs. A literal rendering like “one who came from his genital organs” would be regarded as too specific and perhaps even vulgar by many contemporary readers. Most modern translations thus render the phrase “one of his descendants.”
An allusion to Ps 132:11 and 2 Sam 7:12-13, the promise in the Davidic covenant.

verses.zh: 就预先看明这事，讲论基督复活说：他的灵魂不撇在阴间；他的肉身也不见朽坏。
verses.en: David by foreseeing this[NOTE:1] spoke about the resurrection of the Christ,[NOTE:2] that he was neither abandoned to Hades,[NOTE:3] nor did his body[NOTE:4] experience[NOTE:5] decay.[NOTE:6]
notes: Grk “David foreseeing spoke.” The participle προϊδών (proidōn) is taken as indicating means. It could also be translated as a participle of attendant circumstance: “David foresaw [this] and spoke.” The word “this” is supplied in either case as an understood direct object (direct objects in Greek were often omitted, but must be supplied for the modern English reader).

The term χριστός (christos) was originally an adjective (“anointed”), developing in LXX into a substantive (“an anointed one”), then developing still further into a technical generic term (“the anointed one”). In the intertestamental period it developed further into a technical term referring to the hoped-for anointed one, that is, a specific individual. In the NT the development starts there (technical-specific), is so used in the gospels, and then develops in Paul’s letters to mean virtually Jesus’ last name.tn Or “the Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”
Or “abandoned in the world of the dead.” The translation “world of the dead” for Hades is suggested by L&N 1.19. The phrase is an allusion to Ps 16:10.

Grk “flesh.” See vv. 26b-27. The reference to “body” in this verse picks up the reference to “body” in v. 26. The Greek term σάρξ (sarx) in both verses literally means “flesh”; however, the translation “body” stresses the lack of decay of his physical body. The point of the verse is not merely the lack of decay of his flesh alone, but the resurrection of his entire person, as indicated by the previous parallel line “he was not abandoned to Hades.”
Grk “see,” but the literal translation of the phrase “see decay” could be misunderstood to mean simply “look at decay,” while here “see decay” is really figurative for “experience decay.”
An allusion to Ps 16:10.

verses.zh: 这耶稣，　神已经叫他复活了，我们都为这事作见证。
verses.en: This Jesus God raised up, and we are all witnesses of it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “of him”; Grk “of which [or whom] we are all witnesses” (Acts 1:8).

verses.zh: 他既被　神的右手高举（或译：他既高举在　神的右边），又从父受了所应许的圣灵，就把你们所看见所听见的，浇灌下来。
verses.en: So then, exalted[NOTE:1] to the right hand[NOTE:2] of God, and having received[NOTE:3] the promise of the Holy Spirit[NOTE:4] from the Father, he has poured out[NOTE:5] what you both see and hear.
notes: The aorist participle ὑψωθείς (hupsōtheis) could be taken temporally: “So then, after he was exalted…” In the translation the more neutral “exalted” (a shorter form of “having been exalted”) was used to preserve the ambiguity of the original Greek.
The expression the right hand of God represents supreme power and authority. Its use here sets up the quotation of Ps 110:1 in v. 34.

The aorist participle λαβών (labōn) could be taken temporally: “So then, after he was exalted…and received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit.” In the translation the more neutral “having received” was used to preserve the ambiguity of the original Greek.
Here the genitive τοῦ πνεύματος (tou pneumatos) is a genitive of apposition; the promise consists of the Holy Spirit.
The use of the verb poured out looks back to 2:17-18, where the same verb occurs twice.

verses.zh: 大卫并没有升到天上，但自己说：主对我主说：你坐在我的右边，
verses.en: For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself says, ‘The Lord said to my lord,“Sit[NOTE:1] at my right hand
notes: Sit at my right hand. The word “sit” alludes back to the promise of “seating one on his throne” in v. 30.

verses.zh: 等我使你仇敌作你的脚凳。
verses.en: until I make your enemies a footstool[NOTE:1] for your feet.”’[NOTE:2]
notes: The metaphor make your enemies a footstool portrays the complete subjugation of the enemies.
A quotation from Ps 110:1, one of the most often-cited OT passages in the NT, pointing to the exaltation of Jesus.

verses.zh: 「故此，以色列全家当确实地知道，你们钉在十字架上的这位耶稣，　神已经立他为主，为基督了。」
verses.en: Therefore let all the house of Israel know beyond a doubt[NOTE:1] that God has made this Jesus whom you crucified[NOTE:2] both Lord[NOTE:3] and Christ.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “know for certain.” This term is in an emphatic position in the clause.

Grk “has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.” The clause has been simplified in the translation by replacing the pronoun “him” with the explanatory clause “this Jesus whom you crucified” which comes at the end of the sentence.

Lord. This looks back to the quotation of Ps 110:1 and the mention of “calling on the Lord” in 2:21. Peter’s point is that the Lord on whom one calls for salvation is Jesus because he is the one mediating God’s blessing of the Spirit as a sign of the presence of salvation and the last days.
Or “and Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn See the note on Christ in 2:31.

verses.zh: 众人听见这话，觉得扎心，就对彼得和其余的使徒说：「弟兄们，我们当怎样行？」
verses.en: Now when they heard this,[NOTE:1] they were acutely distressed[NOTE:2] and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “What should we do, brothers?”
notes: The word “this” is not in the Greek text. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek, but must be supplied for the modern English reader.
Grk “they were pierced to the heart” (an idiom for acute emotional distress).

verses.zh: 彼得说：「你们各人要悔改，奉耶稣基督的名受洗，叫你们的罪得赦，就必领受所赐的圣灵；
verses.en: Peter said to them, “Repent, and each one of you be baptized[NOTE:1] in the name of Jesus Christ[NOTE:2] for[NOTE:3] the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.[NOTE:4]
notes: The verb is a third person imperative, but the common translation “let each of you be baptized” obscures the imperative force in English, since it sounds more like a permissive (“each of you may be baptized”) to the average English reader.

In the name of Jesus Christ. Baptism in Messiah Jesus’ name shows how much authority he possesses.tn Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”

There is debate over the meaning of εἰς in the prepositional phrase εἰς ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ὑμῶν (eis aphesin tōn hamartiōn humōn, “for/because of/with reference to the forgiveness of your sins”). Although a causal sense has been argued, it is difficult to maintain here. ExSyn 369-71 discusses at least four other ways of dealing with the passage: (1) The baptism referred to here is physical only, and εἰς has the meaning of “for” or “unto.” Such a view suggests that salvation is based on works—an idea that runs counter to the theology of Acts, namely: (a) repentance often precedes baptism (cf. Acts 3:19; 26:20), and (b) salvation is entirely a gift of God, not procured via water baptism (Acts 10:43 [cf. v. 47]; 13:38-39, 48; 15:11; 16:30-31; 20:21; 26:18); (2) The baptism referred to here is spiritual only. Although such a view fits well with the theology of Acts, it does not fit well with the obvious meaning of “baptism” in Acts—especially in this text (cf. 2:41); (3) The text should be repunctuated in light of the shift from second person plural to third person singular back to second person plural again. The idea then would be, “Repent for/with reference to your sins, and let each one of you be baptized…” Such a view is an acceptable way of handling εἰς, but its subtlety and awkwardness count against it; (4) Finally, it is possible that to a first-century Jewish audience (as well as to Peter), the idea of baptism might incorporate both the spiritual reality and the physical symbol. That Peter connects both closely in his thinking is clear from other passages such as Acts 10:47 and 11:15-16. If this interpretation is correct, then Acts 2:38 is saying very little about the specific theological relationship between the symbol and the reality, only that historically they were viewed together. One must look in other places for a theological analysis. For further discussion see R. N. Longenecker, “Acts,” EBC 9:283-85; B. Witherington, Acts, 154-55; F. F. Bruce, The Acts of the Apostles: The Greek Text with Introduction and Commentary, 129-30; BDAG 290 s.v. εἰς 4.f.
Here the genitive τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος (tou hagiou pneumatos) is a genitive of apposition; the gift consists of the Holy Spirit.

verses.zh: 因为这应许是给你们和你们的儿女，并一切在远方的人，就是主―我们　神所召来的。」
verses.en: For the promise[NOTE:1] is for you and your children, and for all who are far away, as many as the Lord our God will call to himself.”
notes: The promise refers to the promise of the Holy Spirit that Jesus received from the Father in 2:33 and which he now pours out on others. The promise consists of the Holy Spirit (see note in 2:33). Jesus is the active mediator of God’s blessing.

verses.zh: 彼得还用许多话作见证，劝勉他们说：「你们当救自己脱离这弯曲的世代。」
verses.en: With many other words he testified[NOTE:1] and exhorted them saying, “Save yourselves from this perverse[NOTE:2] generation!”
notes: Or “warned.”
Or “crooked” (in a moral or ethical sense). See Luke 3:5.

verses.zh: 于是领受他话的人就受了洗。那一天，门徒约添了三千人，
verses.en: So those who accepted[NOTE:1] his message[NOTE:2] were baptized, and that day about 3,000 people[NOTE:3] were added.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “who acknowledged the truth of.”
Grk “word.”
Grk “souls” (here an idiom for the whole person).
Or “were won over.”

verses.zh: 都恒心遵守使徒的教训，彼此交接，擘饼，祈祷。
verses.en: They were devoting themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship,[NOTE:1] to the breaking of bread and to prayer.[NOTE:2]
notes: Fellowship refers here to close association involving mutual involvement and relationships.
Grk “prayers.” This word was translated as a collective singular in keeping with English style.

verses.zh: 众人都惧怕；使徒又行了许多奇事神迹。
verses.en: Reverential awe[NOTE:1] came over everyone,[NOTE:2] and many wonders and miraculous signs[NOTE:3] came about by the apostles.
notes: Or “Fear.”
Grk “on every soul” (here “soul” is an idiom for the whole person).
In this context the miraculous nature of these signs is implied. Cf. BDAG 920 s.v. σημεῖον 2.a.

verses.zh: 信的人都在一处，凡物公用，
verses.en: All who believed were together and held[NOTE:1] everything in common,
notes: Grk “had.”

verses.zh: 并且卖了田产、家业，照各人所需用的分给各人。
verses.en: and they began selling[NOTE:1] their property[NOTE:2] and possessions and distributing the proceeds[NOTE:3] to everyone, as anyone had need.
notes: The imperfect verb has been translated as an ingressive (“began…”). Since in context this is a description of the beginning of the community of believers, it is more likely that these statements refer to the start of various activities and practices that the early church continued for some time.

It is possible that the first term for property (κτήματα, ktēmata) refers to real estate (as later usage seems to indicate) while the second term (ὑπάρξεις, huparxeis) refers to possessions in general, but it may also be that the two terms are used together for emphasis, simply indicating that all kinds of possessions were being sold. However, if the first term is more specifically a reference to real estate, it foreshadows the incident with Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5:1-11.
Grk “distributing them” (αὐτά, auta). The referent (the proceeds of the sales) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他们天天同心合意恒切地在殿里，且在家中擘饼，存着欢喜、诚实的心用饭，
verses.en: Every day[NOTE:1] they continued to gather together by common consent in the temple courts,[NOTE:2] breaking bread from[NOTE:3] house to house, sharing their food with glad[NOTE:4] and humble hearts,[NOTE:5]
notes: BDAG 437 s.v. ἡμέρα 2.c has “every day” for this phrase.
Grk “in the temple.” This is actually a reference to the courts surrounding the temple proper, and has been translated accordingly.
Here κατά (kata) is used as a distributive (BDAG 512 s.v. B.1.d).
The term glad (Grk “gladness”) often refers to joy brought about by God’s saving acts (Luke 1:14, 44; also the related verb in 1:47; 10:21).

Grk “with gladness and humbleness of hearts.” It is best to understand καρδίας (kardias) as an attributed genitive, with the two nouns it modifies actually listing attributes of the genitive noun which is related to them.

verses.zh: 赞美　神，得众民的喜爱。主将得救的人天天加给他们。
verses.en: praising God and having the good will[NOTE:1] of all the people. And the Lord was adding to their number every day[NOTE:2] those who were being saved.
notes: Or “the favor.”
BDAG 437 s.v. ἡμέρα 2.c has “every day” for this phrase.
